header.name: relay
header.tagline: Every run leaves a certificate a stranger can check offline.

flows.kicker: one run, handed to a stranger
flows.title: How a coding run becomes something you can check without trusting it
flows.footnote: Refuted outranks unverifiable, and both outrank allow. A doubt is never a pass.
flows.alt: Eight stages of an accountable coding run: goal, context, tool call, anchored edit, ledger, check, bisect, certificate. The goal is pinned as the first row of a hash-chained ledger. Project conventions and a bounded repo map fold into the prompt verbatim. Every tool call is permission-checked before it runs, and an anchored edit that does not match exactly once writes nothing. The acceptance check runs outside anything the model can call. A bisect replays the recorded edits until the check goes red, naming the first breaking edit. The certificate is a few kilobytes and re-derives with no model and no network. Three outcomes: allow, refuted, and unverifiable.

stages.title: Goal
stages.note: The task, pinned as the first row of the ledger.

stages.title: Context
stages.note: Your conventions file and a bounded repo map, verbatim.

stages.title: Tool call
stages.note: The model proposes; permission is checked before it runs.

stages.title: Anchored edit
stages.note: The target must match once, or nothing is written.

stages.title: Ledger
stages.note: Every turn, call, and result appends to a hash chain.

stages.title: Check
stages.note: Your acceptance command, outside anything the model can call.

stages.title: Bisect
stages.note: Replay the recorded edits until the check goes red.

stages.title: Certificate
stages.note: A few kilobytes, re-derived with no model and no network.

returns.label: THE CHECK RUNS AGAIN ON EACH REPLAYED EDIT

outcomes.label: ALLOW
outcomes.note: chain intact, receipts re-derive, contract met

outcomes.label: REFUTED
outcomes.note: a broken chain, or a claim the record denies

outcomes.label: UNVERIFIABLE
outcomes.note: a clause this verifier cannot re-derive

flows.title: How a request reaches a model without forging anything to get there
flows.footnote: The ladder only moves one way. A missing credential drops a rung, and nothing is forged.
flows.alt: Eight stages of the endpoint ladder: prompt, ladder, served local, Ollama, subscription, public API, gateway, cloud. Rungs are tried in order, with free and private tiers first, so metered tokens are spent only when the local ones are unavailable. A subscription rung uses the official command-line tool's own login. A gateway rung uses only its own dedicated key and never replays the provider's official credential to a third-party URL. A rung whose credential is absent is never added to the ladder at all. Three outcomes: answered, ladder exhausted, and nothing to try.

stages.title: Prompt
stages.note: One request, and no tier named by hand.

stages.title: Ladder
stages.note: Rungs in order, free and private ones first.

stages.title: Served local
stages.note: A model served on this machine, offline and unmetered.

stages.title: Ollama
stages.note: The largest model already pulled here, still local.

stages.title: Subscription
stages.note: The official CLI, using the login you already hold.

stages.title: Public API
stages.note: A provider key read from your own environment.

stages.title: Gateway
stages.note: A base URL you set, with its own dedicated key.

stages.title: Cloud
stages.note: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint, the last rung tried.

outcomes.label: ANSWERED
outcomes.note: the first live rung replied, and stopped there

outcomes.label: LADDER EXHAUSTED
outcomes.note: every rung present was tried, and none replied

outcomes.label: NOTHING TO TRY
outcomes.note: no credential present, so no rung was offered
